about.title: Patterson Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Patterson sits along busy Stanislaus County corridors like Sperry Avenue, 2nd Street, Las Palmas Avenue, and Route 33, where the most recent full-year count logged 51 injury collisions and 82 people injured. Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. see the heaviest reported crash activity, likely tied to commuter traffic and weekend travel through town. When a crash happens here, the aftermath can be disorienting: medical appointments, missed work, vehicle repairs, and calls from insurance adjusters all arrive at once. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect injured Patterson residents with independent personal injury attorneys who understand local roads and California's claims process. There's no cost to get connected, and no obligation to move forward. The goal is to help you get organized and get informed while decisions still matter, without added pressure or fees upfront.

whyChoose.title: Why Patterson Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Time Limits Matter
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a lawsuit, but claims against a government entity (like a road defect claim against the city or county) can require notice in as little as six months. Acting early helps preserve your options.

items.title: Fault Sharing Won't Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for the crash, though your share of fault reduces the amount. An attorney can help make sure your percentage of fault is argued fairly.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront fee and no payment unless you recover.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters often use those statements to minimize what they owe, even innocent phrasing can be used against you later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened at a Patterson intersection with no clear fault?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue compensation even if fault is shared or unclear, including at corridors like Sperry Avenue or Las Palmas Avenue. An attorney can help gather evidence, such as traffic camera footage or witness statements, to clarify what happened.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to hire anyone after you're connected.
